scope: Phase 3 edge routing spike — sanitized observation source of record
provenanceRules: Every observation names the deployment it was actually taken from.
Controlled-failure deployments, binding transitions, and production read-only observations are never relabeled as the final selected Worker version.
No account identifiers, zone identifiers, secret values, signed URLs, or preview hostnames appear in this file.

deploymentTimeline.role: Route-transfer rehearsal. Not the final selected version.

deploymentTimeline.label: spike:controlled-failure
deploymentTimeline.role: Deliberate missing-binding failure used to prove protected routes fail closed instead of falling through to site assets. Not the final selected version.

deploymentTimeline.label: spike:reverse-binding
deploymentTimeline.role: Reverse binding of the staging custom domain. Establishes the staging half of composite rollback.

deploymentTimeline.label: retained-candidate-b
deploymentTimeline.deploymentMessage: Harden edge streaming and error isolation
deploymentTimeline.role: The retained selected staging edge. All rows in edge-routing-reprobe.json carry this version id.

deploymentTimeline.label: incident:site-spike-domain-takeover
deploymentTimeline.role: A fixture-bound site stand-in deployed during Phase 3 source reconstruction. It took the staging custom domain from vcskill-site-staging.
deploymentTimeline.resolution: The custom domain was detached and reattached to vcskill-site-staging, and vcskill-site-spike was deleted. Post-restoration probes match the pre-incident behavior. Recorded here because the transition is part of this endpoint's real provenance, not a clean history.

bindingTransitions.mechanism: detach custom domain, then reattach to the prior owner
bindingTransitions.detail: Staging binding reversal succeeded and the endpoint returned to its retained behavior: site HTML at /, edge contract on the four protected route patterns.

productionObservations.detail: Production stayed healthy under its existing credential context throughout Phase 3. No production route, domain, Worker, or secret was changed.

failedProbesRetained.detail: The exact legacy source returned 401 for /install when rehearsed on staging under the new consolidated credential, while the unchanged production legacy deployment continued to return 200 under its own credential context.
failedProbesRetained.reason: Preserved explicitly. A failed staging probe is never counted as rollback success; composite rollback proof requires staging binding reversal plus read-only production compatibility.

principalRoleGate.detail: Draft releases are visible only to a principal with push access; that role requirement is satisfied.

tokenPermissionGate.required: one fine-grained PAT scoped only to bavanchun/vcskill with Contents read and Actions write, and without Contents/release/administration write
tokenPermissionGate.observed: no such token exists in this environment; the available credential is a broad classic OAuth token whose scope exceeds the approved consolidation
tokenPermissionGate.detail: This consolidation was operator-approved as an exception and must not be represented as least privilege. It is not provisioned yet.

draftAccessPreflight.deferredTo: Phase 9 must prove actual held-draft visibility before release synchronization. Phase 3 records the permission gate only.

candidateA.reason: Route patterns are matched against the full URL including the query string and cannot themselves contain a query, so admitting /install?from=docs requires the terminal wildcard /install*. That wildcard also captures the unprotected lookalike /installer. Under a pure Candidate A split the captured lookalike would reach an edge Worker with no way to return the frozen site behavior through a non-recursive site path, so the gate fails.

candidateB.reason: One combined Worker owns the protected routes and delegates every unprotected path, including wildcard-captured lookalikes, to its ASSETS binding. Exact route classification happens before any decoding or fallback, so a colliding static file cannot pre-empt a protected route and a protected error never reaches the asset layer.

openFailures.cause: The source-owned raw dot-segment ingress rule is not applied to the zone.
openFailures.impact: Cloudflare normalizes dot segments before the Worker reads Request.url, so /download/./checksums.txt resolves to a real asset and /download/../secrets.txt resolves to a site 404. Neither reaches the Worker in its raw form, and in-Worker validation therefore cannot observe or reject the raw shape.
openFailures.blockedBy: a Cloudflare API token with Zone -> WAF -> Edit
